creatures.name: Tin Hinan the Shade

powers.name: Donning the Corporeal Veil
powers.description: Takes on a material form (Lesser Power, -5 Might cost).

powers.name: Focus Power (Divination)
powers.description: Up to 7 points: Intellego Corpus, Imaginem or Vim effects up to 7th magnitude. Its Initiative is the magnitude - 3.

powers.name: Focus Power (Destruction)
powers.description: Up to 7 points: Perdo Animal, Corpus or Terram effects up to 7th magnitude. Its Initiative is the magnitude - 3.

powers.name: Invisibility
powers.description: She, or someone she touches, turns invisible at will, though Second Sight still sees her. The effect is PeIm 15; the book also says the Lesser Power's 25 levels.

powers.name: Ritual Focus Power (Healing)
powers.description: Up to 7 points: Creo Corpus ritual effects up to 7th magnitude, paid for with any fitting vis she holds. Its Initiative is (2 x magnitude) - 3.

creatures.appearance: A breathtaking, raven-haired Berber woman of noble bearing, sitting cross-legged with her legs covered, in white and blue robes, her lips and eyelids blue.
creatures.notes:
Tin Hinan rose in the Atlas, and a prophetic dream sent her across the desert on a white camel laden with millet and dates, her servant Takama with her. She found the land empty and made her seat at Abalessa, where she bore three daughters, Tinhert (antelope), Temerwelt (hare) and Tahenkot (gazelle), who founded the royal tribes of the Imazighen and Tuareg. From Takama came the servile caste.

Even death did not part her from her people: her shade is bound to the desert, answers the Brides of Ayyur, and will stay as long as the tribes seek her out. Her one great aim is to help and protect the Imazighen. She crosses vast distances by night through the Magic regiones of the Great Desert, and keeps some of her old destructive powers, no longer needing amulets for them.

Her Driven is to protect and perpetuate the Tuareg, printed as her first Flaw. While her body lies undisturbed she uses Extractor of Corpus Vis to draw 5 Corpus pawns a season from the aura, her tomb serving as her laboratory, and may hold up to 20 for her Ritual Focus Power.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 93

creatures.name: Toaten (Ant-Folk)

powers.name: Delve the Earth
powers.description: With a touch, a tunnel a pace deep. Used over and over to build warrens, and to loosen stones for the great burial mounds (PeTe; 2 mastery points on Might cost, 1 on Initiative).

creatures.equipment: Any small thing that caught its interest, a camel-hide loincloth, and a sling wound round the waist or worn as a sash with a stone ready.
creatures.appearance: Between ant and dwarf, no taller than a young child: hairless, carapace-like ochre skin, two pairs of arms ending in rough claws, large black eyes without pupils, and two jutting lower tusks for breaking stone. Almost always filthy.
creatures.notes:
Not quite monsters, but of the Otherworld. They call themselves helpful servants of the Dii Mauri and work tirelessly in swarms, rebuilding the mountains the lowhush keep eroding. By an ancient compact they raise and keep the sacred tombs of the Berbers. Those who barter strange goods with them can hire their labour. They love fruit and wine, but drunk toaten work badly.

Individuals might have one more Virtue and Flaw. Their Weakness is Fresh Fruit or Wine.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 126

creatures.name: Teryel
creatures.notes:
The teryelen are primeval ogresses, daughters of the Teryel, first woman and first witch of the Berber creation. Rather like the ghul of Bedouin tales, a teryel may be a night terror many times over, and sometimes a saviour of women suffering violence. The greatest wield magic like the highest Court Faeries of Europe: African Great Lezis, landholders of the wasteland and keepers of great treasures.

Faerie, one of the lowhush of the amadagh. The book prints no statistics for it.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 127

creatures.name: Aicha Bouteliss
creatures.notes:

creatures.name: Ba'al Ammon, Lord of Carthage
creatures.weakness: Protected Group: people who have sacrificed to the Punic Gods that day.

powers.name: Form of Fancy
powers.description: Once in a body, he shifts to any human form, even with animal parts such as curling ram's horns, and dissolves them at will. A natural change: Magic Resistance does not stop physical attacks.

powers.name: Know the Places of Men
powers.description: Up to 10 points, a point a magnitude: Intellego Corpus or Imaginem effects up to 10th magnitude.

powers.name: Master of Flame
powers.description: Up to 10 points, a point a magnitude: Ignem effects up to 10th magnitude.

powers.name: Summon the Herd of Destruction
powers.description: A ritual power (ReMe 15, +4 Arc, +3 Moon, +2 Group): 10 ghostly war elephants who obey him, or one he names, for Moon Duration. They understand only Punic.

powers.name: Coagulation
powers.description: Takes a material form, which he may dissolve at will.

powers.name: Envisioning
powers.description: 1 point to appear in a sleeper's dreams, 5 for a waking dream. So he often spoke to his worshippers.

powers.name: His Master's Voice
powers.description: Variable: summons demons or corrupt beasts to him, 1 point for each point of their Infernal Might, so rarely used. He has no control over what comes.

powers.name: Obsession
powers.description: 1 to 3 points: imposes the Obsession Traits of Greed, Merciless Ambition and Pride (Realms of Power: The Infernal pp. 31-32).

powers.name: Possession
powers.description: Variable: as Realms of Power: The Infernal. Might moved into a Possession Pool stays there until the possession ends. The more Might, the more he can do and the weaker the Penetration. Each portion is an independent copy of his mind using any Power its pool can pay for. He may give the host Magic Resistance equal to the Pool, or hide within and pass wards. Forcing the host, or using its powers, draws on the pool (1 point a magnitude or Ability point, or the Might the victim spent; a questionable act must beat the host's Trait on stress die + Might spent). The possession ends at pool 0. Vim spells drain the pool but must Penetrate his full Might.

powers.name: Shroud the Stench of the Pit
powers.description: Variable: conceals the Infernal nature of a power or aura as Magical or Faerie, or as wholly mundane, even from Sense Holiness and Unholiness, for as long as what it masks. It costs the masked Power's cost, or its magnitude if it costs no Might.

powers.name: Wealth of Nations
powers.description: Summons riches of intrinsic value up to 50 pounds of gold from somewhere else, a royal treasury or the purse of the man beside you, chosen to corrupt most.

vis.where: vis infesta, carried on long stays abroad

creatures.appearance: A handsome, well and fittingly dressed man or woman, curling ram's horns at the sides of his head, eyes like cinders, and always a large, vicious sword. He takes the look and sex the summoner would find most fitting. A snake always comes with him, sometimes a small garter or viper, sometimes something larger.
creatures.notes:
Lord of the Punic pantheon and patron of Carthage, his sign the ram's spiral horns; nominally a moon god. The Egyptians linked him to Amun, the Greeks to Kronos, who fathered the Younger Titans that so intrigued the Founder Tytalus, swallowed the first Olympians, and sacrificed his son Iarbus for victory. He answered nobles' prayers in war with ghostly elephants and soldiers, and made the fiery artillery of the living burn with Hell's hunger. He survived as the Roman Ba'al Saturn. A potent necromancer and master of flame.

He delights in corrupting men, in death and destruction, and in driving societies down. By Vis Mastery he spends vis as Might, and carries several rooks of it when long manifested.

The book promises the ghostly war elephants' statistics 'later' and does not print them.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa pp. 133-134
creatures.secrets: He is one demon of Hell who played every god of the Punics, and at last revealed himself to the Goetics as Baalzebub. The vast cache of vis infesta outside Tunis is his.

creatures.name: The Jealous Wife

powers.name: Possession
powers.description: For 1 or more points, if it penetrates, the victim is possessed and under her direct control. Using the host's magic costs 1 Might per magnitude; a questionable act against the host's nature needs a stress die + Might spent over the host's Personality Trait roll (see Entrancement, ArM5 p. 65, for modifiers), and both costs apply together. Under her direct control the host has her Magic Resistance and is stopped by wards against her; acting freely, the host has neither. The costs follow Realms of Power: Magic, not Hermetic magic.

vis.where: in the fingernails of the possession victim

creatures.equipment: Someone else's body and all her goods.
creatures.appearance: She has no body of her own. Faerie Sight, or Second Sight outside a body, shows a furious face floating like a mask before the victim's head.
creatures.notes:
This faerie possesses a woman who falls from her husband's favour when another wife has good fortune, and so cannot live in a house where wives are treated alike. She sometimes poisons and sometimes seems unable to, which may mean there are several. Choosing not to kill, she keeps raising and lowering wives in the husband's eyes, possessing each in turn. Her traits are appearances: she has lost nothing herself, and chooses women with cause and acts as she thinks would be interesting.

Printed Virtues and Flaws: Focus Faerie Powers (Possession), 2 x Increased Might, Loosely Material (as a Minor Virtue, forms only by possession); Incognizant. Her Strength, Stamina, Dexterity, Quickness and Size, and her fingernail attack, are the host's. Her Pretenses are Intrigue 5 (servants), and she may use the host's Abilities. The book prints her OK to Unconscious ladder under Wound Penalties. Not suited to be a player character.

Wound ranges: Light 1-5, Medium to 10, Heavy to 15, Incapacitated to 20, Dead from 21.

creatures.notes:
A hot, dry and dusty wind that usually blows out of the south for fifty days, from after Easter until Pentecost. It carries dust, sand and terrible plagues, and spreads them gladly.

One of the Council of Winds. The book prints no statistics for it.

creatures.name: The Simoon
creatures.appearance: A barely veiled woman who loves to dance: passionate, capricious and cruel without thinking of it.
creatures.notes:

One of the Council of Winds. The book prints no statistics for it.

creatures.name: Magical Bouda
creatures.how_many: Packs led by women; rumour tells of whole villages

params.power: Trembling Fear of the Predator's Gaze

powers.name: Deceitful Tongue
powers.description: Its Initiative is Qik + 3. Any voice of man or creature, in any language it knows, in any shape (MuIm).

powers.name: Trembling Fear of the Predator's Gaze
powers.description: Its Initiative is Qik - 2. While it holds his eye the target cannot run or dodge, though he can use his hands or call out; he loses his Quickness from Defense and takes -3 (ReCo).

powers.name: Rending Fangs
powers.description: A common power. Its Initiative is Qik - 3. Its bite destroys leather, bone, wood, cloth, stone or metal it can get its teeth round. With an attack it takes a point of Protection off armour, or instead of one it breaks a weapon or shield if it beats Defense by 3 or more, doing no damage; not together with Ripping Jaws (PeTe(An, He)).

powers.name: Ripping Jaws
powers.description: A common power. Its Initiative is Qik - 2. The victim takes -3 to all recovery rolls until fully healed, for any wound; Incapacitating Wounds leave scars that never fade (PeCo).

powers.name: The Beast Between
powers.description: A common power. 3 points or Fatigue; Initiative Qik - 2. A hyena's head, claws, fur and tail on a man's upright frame, human mental Characteristics and a hyena's physical ones, usable hands, Protection +2. Bite of the hybrid form: Init 0, Attack +3, Defense +1, Damage +4. Ended early by changing shape (MuCo, free Animal requisite).

creatures.appearance: Often red-tinged eyes, a very hairy body, a nasal voice and foul breath. In human form it casts a hyena's shadow. Tame animals hate it and will not be touched.
creatures.notes:
Shapeshifting hyena-men of the Maghreb and the Tell who love to prey on children, a magical kin of Animal and Corpus (Realms of Power: Magic p. 89). They live and hunt easily as men or hyenas, most changing only at night and returning at dawn; the strongest take a hybrid shape. Even as hyenas they speak with human voices, and so draw the unwary in. A pack can keep a district in constant fear for anyone outdoors, and secret lovers often fall to them.

Inherited Virtues: Deceitful Tongue, Trembling Fear, Skinchanger (needing no item, hyena only and at night only), Wilderness Sense. Common Virtues: Rending Fangs, Ripping Jaws, The Beast Between. Common Flaws: Driven (terrorizing communities, Major), Dark Secret, Offensive to Animals. No Characteristics or Might are printed.

Folklore's werehyena is at least Size +1 (Large), hairy and hunch-backed, its hind legs shorter than its forelegs, with glowing red eyes (p. 118). Many North African jinn, Faerie and Infernal, also take the hyena's shape and are mistaken for bouda.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa pp. 116-118

creatures.name: Faerie Bouda (Werehyena)
creatures.how_many: From Morocco to the Sudan, living among the villages

powers.name: Blacksmithing
powers.description: Or Crafter's Healing, below. 1 point a magnitude, Initiative variable: any non-Ritual Creo, Muto, Rego or Perdo Terram spell, within its motif as a blacksmith.

powers.name: Crafter's Healing
powers.description: In place of Blacksmithing, as the Major Supernatural Virtue (City & Guild p. 71).

powers.name: Looked at Thrice
powers.description: As Trembling Fear of the Predator's Gaze.

powers.name: The Shadow Stays the Hound
powers.description: Paralyzes a dog the werehyena's shadow falls on (Base 5, +2 Sight, +1 Conc).

powers.name: Transform into Human
powers.description: Human form for Duration: Sun, and only at sunrise (Personal, MuAn(Co)).

creatures.appearance: As a man: a disturbing smell, a nasal voice, an ugly hairy body.
creatures.notes:
A dark faerie that wears a human shape by day, as blacksmith, healer or wizard, and goes back to the hyena by night to rob graves. Though only narrowly cognizant it is clever, and grows Pretenses to fit the villages it secretly plagues, copying the magical bouda. Unlike most faeries it feels pain, fatigue and hunger as its neighbours do. Its Abilities are Pretenses.

Built as a strong companion or weak magus, with 6 points of Virtues and 3 of Flaws unassigned. Lesser kinds lack some powers; greater ones have Entrancement, more smithing magic such as Touched by the Faerie Realm, and other mind-control or shapeshifting powers. Its block lists Crafter's Healing or Focus Power (Blacksmithing) as alternatives; Crafter's Healing stands here. A hyena's bite is Init 0, Atk +4, Def +1, Dam +3.

Bouda Blood (p. 117), the Faerie Blood of its descendants: +1 to Strength or Intelligence, to no more than +3; Legacy +1, to +4; Sympathies Wastelands, Cruelty, Mimicry; other Virtues and Flaws Entrancement, Puissant Guile, Skinchanger (hyena), Disfigured, Feral Scent; hairless but for the back, hunch-backed, always red-eyed.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 117

creatures.name: Anthropophagus (Man-Eater)
creatures.notes:
A man's shape with a vast pot belly, a mouth crowded with hippopotamus tusks, small piggy eyes and sparse hair. What disgusts its neighbours, though, is the habit of eating its own dead. A member who dies by mishap is ritually consumed by friends and family, unless of a disease, and then only if it clearly touched just one organ. Drinking cups are made of the skulls of each family's most famous, and other body parts are worn. Alone of the Magic Humans they are not tolerated in human settlements, for all their protests that they want only their own.

Tusks: Init 0, Attack +6, Defense +2, Damage +11.

A Magic Human of the Plinian races: Might by the character's role, most Spring, immune to deprivation unless stated, Monstrous Appearance free, speaking its human neighbours' languages (pp. 119-120).
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa pp. 119-120
creatures.secrets:
Their Greater Malediction: Magic auras do not keep off Acclimation. They must eat human flesh in a ceremony at least once a year, or lose a Magic Quality each year until they are ordinary, hideous mortals. One corpse feeds five. A family with no death to hand must make one, and those who tire of it and let themselves acclimate are usually eaten first; the last resort is the nearest human settlement.

Not all are born to it. A human who shares the ceremony gains Transformed Human with the Greater Malediction. A village will sometimes spare a victim, share the secret, and send him home to get them the sacred meal each year. He gains Disfigured after five ceremonies, and after fifteen is too monstrous to stay among men.

creatures.name: Astomus (Mouthless)

powers.name: The Tongueless Voice
powers.description: A constant effect, no cost. Any sound, speech, song or music comes from the head, no louder than a human could make; only suppressing the power silences it (CrIm).

creatures.notes:
The Apple-Smellers have no mouth and need neither breath, food nor drink, taking some sustenance through smell; they often carry apples. A very bad odour is said to kill them, and can certainly lay one low. Soft, silky, pale hair covers them, and they wear cloth of a soft cotton or down harvested from trees. Their voices are high and trilling, and they are superb singers. Frederick Barbarossa kept a choir of three, who soon sickened and died in the European climate.

A Magic Human of the Plinian races: Might by the character's role, most Spring, immune to deprivation unless stated, Monstrous Appearance free, speaking its human neighbours' languages (pp. 119-120).
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa pp. 120-121

creatures.name: Blemmya
creatures.notes:
Merchants who live mostly in the deserts of Libya, with a large tribe on the upper Nile. They make little and bargain superbly, buying low and selling high, and lead camel trains on longer treks than human rivals by being immune to thirst. Their faces are on their chests, with no head or neck, the shoulders set wide and the face larger than a man's; their ears lie beneath their arms, so they hear poorly. They are hairless, go bare above the waist, and are naturally hard to hurt. Armour needs eye holes or a visor, so must be rigid, and large shields are of little use to them; their warriors tend to be mounted skirmishers with slings.

A Magic Human of the Plinian races: Might by the character's role, most Spring, immune to deprivation unless stated, Monstrous Appearance free, speaking its human neighbours' languages (pp. 119-120).
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 121

creatures.name: Cynocephalus (Dog-Head)
creatures.notes:
Dog-headed giants up to ten feet tall, found all along Africa's coast and commonest in Cyrenaica; some say the Canary Islands are named for ancient Dog-Heads. The Eastern Church's lore makes Saint Christopher one, born Reprobus, his fur turning white at baptism. They are covered in coarse black fur, with erect ears and long snouts full of dagger teeth, and smell exceptionally well (+3 to all rolls with scent, trails included). Many have Afflicted Tongue, though their own kind understand them. Men and women alike hunt antelope and wild goat with spears, and now and then take livestock. They eat meat raw, wear skins, and trade skins and leather for wool, pots and consumables. Most are pagan, worshipping jnun and spirits, and the Arab and Muslim dislike of dogs falls on them too.

A Magic Human of the Plinian races: Might by the character's role, most Spring, immune to deprivation unless stated, Monstrous Appearance free, speaking its human neighbours' languages (pp. 119-120).
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa pp. 121-122

creatures.name: Maritimus

powers.name: Double Sighted
powers.description: A constant effect, no cost. He makes out detail at any distance as if a foot away, and judges distance to an inch or so at several miles (InIm, Personal Power x2).

creatures.notes:
A race with a second set of eyes above the first, keen-sighted and expert archers. One eye, it is said, looks to God to live rightly, one to the world to avoid sin, one to the Devil to flee him and one to the flesh to punish it. Nearly all have been Christian since the days of the Vandals, though not all good ones: now and then one serves as lookout on a Barbary pirate. Most live on the coasts of Mauritania, fishing and gathering shellfish.

A Magic Human of the Plinian races: Might by the character's role, most Spring, immune to deprivation unless stated, Monstrous Appearance free, speaking its human neighbours' languages (pp. 119-120).
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 122

creatures.name: Panotius (All-Ear)

powers.name: Auricular Flight
powers.description: Its Initiative is Qik - 2. A short-term Fatigue level for flight as fast as a running horse. Every minute a Stamina + Concentration roll against 6 or another Fatigue level; none when Dazed. Athletics steers (ReCo).

creatures.notes:
A timid, peaceful race, milk-white of skin, with ears that reach the ground and are looped round the arms to keep them out of the dirt. They fold them round their bodies for warmth and spread them as wings. Otherwise they look and dress like the humans about them. They grow fruit trees in secluded valleys and oases, best under high cliffs, eat no meat, work no metal, and are sought for their knowledge of legend and lore. Most have Noncombatant, and fly to a high perch from any fight.

A Magic Human of the Plinian races: Might by the character's role, most Spring, immune to deprivation unless stated, Monstrous Appearance free, speaking its human neighbours' languages (pp. 119-120).
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 122

creatures.name: Tripithamus

powers.name: The Sun's Glance
powers.description: A constant effect, no cost. The eyes shine like a lantern for five paces, without hurting sight; only closing them or a Confidence point shuts it off (CrIg; printed Greater Power, 10 levels, -2 cost).

powers.name: The Sun's Breath
powers.description: Its Initiative is Qik - 1. Heats a thing no bigger than her head: metal glows red, water boils, the flammable ignites. It cools normally (CrIg).

powers.name: The Sun's Shout
powers.description: Its Initiative is Qik + 1. Spits a dart of fire for +5 damage if it Penetrates (CrIg).

creatures.notes:
Three spans high (27 inches), from the far south at the edge of the torrid zone; also called Pygmaei. The sun has charred their skins black, and they hold its heat and light. Instead of clothes they braid their long hair with grasses and beads. They are mostly pagan, raising shrines to fire and the sun; they grow crops and keep little cattle for milk and normal goats or ostriches to ride. Their society is matriarchal: in some tribes the men are little more than slaves, in others nearly equals. They war forever with a race of supernatural cranes who steal their grain.

Warriors carry a copper sword, made by the tribe's priests, that bursts into flame when drawn and works only for a tripithamus: a short sword (ArM5 p. 176) with +3 Initiative and +6 Damage. Their Improved Damage and Initiative apply to these swords.

A Magic Human of the Plinian races: Might by the character's role, most Spring, immune to deprivation unless stated, Monstrous Appearance free, speaking its human neighbours' languages (pp. 119-120).
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 122

creatures.name: Troglodyte (Hole-Creeper)

powers.name: Eyes of the Bat
powers.description: A constant effect, no cost. Moves freely in complete darkness, as the Hermetic spell (ArM5 p. 127; InAu).

creatures.notes:
Thin, pale cave-dwellers with tiny eyes that cannot bear bright light and huge pink ears, met when Berber clans who dig their homes broke through into caves lived in since time began. Some meetings end in harmony, the troglodytes in the depths and the Berbers near the entrance; others in a fight until one side is gone. They go naked until they meet humans, then take traded clothes or make them of pale fish skin and mangy rat pelts. None has ever been heard to make a sound. Among themselves they use touch and signs that humans do not know, and trade by simple gestures. They are very fast, as humans mostly learn when they flee the light, and they kill snakes wherever they find them.

A Magic Human of the Plinian races: Might by the character's role, most Spring, immune to deprivation unless stated, Monstrous Appearance free, speaking its human neighbours' languages (pp. 119-120).
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 124

creatures.name: Amyctyra
creatures.notes:
A lower lip that juts so far it shades them like an umbrella. They eat only raw meat and are unfriendly to outsiders.

One of the other monstrous races. The book prints no statistics for it.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 122

creatures.name: Androgynus (Man-Woman)
creatures.notes:
Has the anatomy of both sexes, and a society that knows no gender roles.

One of the other monstrous races. The book prints no statistics for it.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 122

creatures.name: Artibatira
creatures.notes:
Walks on all fours, with shorter legs, longer arms and a longer neck than a human, and cannot speak.

One of the other monstrous races. The book prints no statistics for it.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 122

creatures.name: Erythropodes (Red-Feet)
creatures.notes:
Twenty-four feet tall, arms white to the shoulder, black ears, red feet, round heads and long noses. They live near the river Brixon, a tributary of the Nile.

One of the other monstrous races. The book prints no statistics for it.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 122

creatures.name: Gorillae
creatures.notes:
Hairy humans named by Hanno the Navigator of Carthage, with six fingers on each hand and boar's teeth. In most tribes the men have tails; in some, neither sex has one.

One of the other monstrous races. The book prints no statistics for it.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 122

creatures.name: Hippopod (Horse-Foot)
creatures.notes:
Two long toes like an ostrich's and two broad fingers like a lobster's claws. They run exceptionally fast.

One of the other monstrous races. The book prints no statistics for it.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 122

creatures.name: Monoculus (One-Eye)
creatures.notes:
Often mistaken for a cyclops: the same single eye in the middle of the forehead, without the giant's stature.

One of the other monstrous races. The book prints no statistics for it.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 122

creatures.name: Ghola (African)
creatures.notes:
A large female jinni who changes shape to hide her real form, a hairy, goat-footed ogress like the teryel. A cannibal, she lures prey with soft mimicked voices. Dark faeries like the ghula of other lands (Realms of Power: Faerie p. 71). Some ghouls have the ears and feet of a donkey and the jaws of a jackal (p. 123).

The book prints no statistics for it.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 125

creatures.name: Ghul of the Siwah Necropoli
creatures.notes:
A savager creature of the same name, only in the eastern necropoli of the Siwah Oasis, closer to the creatures of Egypt and the Sinai mountains: a hulking sorcerer that takes the form of a jackal, hyena or vulture. A demonic jinni like the Infernal Ghul of The Cradle and the Crescent p. 73.

The book prints no statistics for it.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 125

creatures.name: Shayatin (The Devils)
creatures.notes:
Wicked invisible spirits of graveyards, ruins, thresholds and latrines, who tempt and corrupt as European demons do. They are the shaitan of the east: corrupt Infernal jinn, equal to the mazzikim, succubi, Evil Spirits and other immaterial demons of Realms of Power: The Infernal. Sihr affects them all.

The book prints no statistics for it.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 125

creatures.name: Leriah (The Jnun of the Air)
creatures.notes:
Disease Spirits, demons that infect their victims through Diseased Possession. There are seven tribes, each tormenting on its own day of the week. They are not true jinn, and Sihr does not touch them.

The book prints no statistics for it.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 125

creatures.name: Sidi Moussa
creatures.notes:
Sultan of the baharia, in the Seventh Depth. He pays homage only to the Sultan al-Hut.

The book prints no statistics for it.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 125

creatures.name: The Sultan al-Hut
creatures.notes:
The Lord of Fishes, a dark and powerful pre-Islamic Faerie deity at the head of a feudal court of sea creatures.

The book prints no statistics for it.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 125

creatures.name: Tanit
creatures.notes:
The Queen of Blood and Fire, consort and confidante of Ba'al Ammon, goddess of war, virgin mother, nurse and sign of fertility, her shrines outnumbering his; she was thought to sway him. Most stelae bear her sign, a circle on a triangle with a line across the point, not unlike an ankh, and she sometimes has a lion's head. The Egyptians tied her to Nit of war and the hunt; the Greeks saw Juno Caelestis, the African Juno.

The book prints no statistics for it.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 135
creatures.secrets: Only a mask. Whatever this god once was, by the fall of Carthage the whole pantheon was one demon, Ba'al Ammon.

creatures.name: Dagon
creatures.notes:
Ruler of farming and fishing and the bounty of the land, the Greeks' Zeus Arotrios. He also guarded the underwater prison of seven titans cast into the sea.

The book prints no statistics for it.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 135
creatures.secrets: Only a mask. Whatever this god once was, by the fall of Carthage the whole pantheon was one demon, Ba'al Ammon.

creatures.name: Eshmun
creatures.notes:
God of healing, linked with Asclepius: eighth son of Sydyk, carrying his staff of office with a snake coiled round his other arm. His brothers were the secretive Cabieri of Samothrace.

The book prints no statistics for it.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 135
creatures.secrets: Only a mask. Whatever this god once was, by the fall of Carthage the whole pantheon was one demon, Ba'al Ammon.

creatures.name: Sydyk
creatures.notes:
Discoverer of the uses of salt and judge of the gods, interpreting when Ba'al Ammon was absent: harsh, unforgiving, valuing righteousness over mercy. Sanchuniathon names his father as Magos, a follower of Zoroaster who rose as a foreign god.

The book prints no statistics for it.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 135
creatures.secrets: Only a mask. Whatever this god once was, by the fall of Carthage the whole pantheon was one demon, Ba'al Ammon.

creatures.name: Melkart
creatures.notes:
The Tyrian Heracles, patron of Tyre and Leptis Magna, god of death and rebirth, protector of his places and his most devout. A legacy of Carthage's birth as a colony of Tyre. Hannibal followed him, Septimius Severus built him a temple in Rome, and his cult spread through the Punic colonies of Iberia.

The book prints no statistics for it.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 135
creatures.secrets: Only a mask. Whatever this god once was, by the fall of Carthage the whole pantheon was one demon, Ba'al Ammon.

creatures.name: Camel, Dromedary (Camelus)
creatures.appearance: A single-humped Arabian camel.
creatures.notes:
The common riding dromedary (Jamal), first given under Alexander of Jerbiton in Magi of Hermes pp. 10-11. Camels smell drinkable water up to two miles off by its air-after-rain scent, go up to two weeks without it and can walk through mild sandstorms unharmed. Splayed feet carry them faster over sand than horses and tire them less.

Riding camel, the mehari of the lower classes' races: add Fast Runner (+3 to running) and Improved Characteristics, Quickness +0. War camel: add Aggressive, Pack Animal and Ferocity (when ridden in battle), Brawl (hooves) 5; kick Init +0, Attack +8, Defense +5, Damage +2; it can train to attack in a Trained Group with its rider. Bactrian camel: Hardy, Long-Winded and Feral Scent, fully given in The Cradle and the Crescent p. 170.

The block's wound ranges stop at Incapacitated 22+.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 136

creatures.name: Camel of Virtue

powers.name: Perfect Form of the Desert Ship
powers.description: Turns it into dromedary or Bactrian form and back, changing its Characteristics and non-magical Qualities to suit (MuAn; Base 5, +2 Sun).

powers.name: Keep the Simoon at Bay
powers.description: Shields the camel, its herd and any riders from the simoon, the scorching wind and sandstorm of the deep desert (ReAu).

powers.name: Scent the Distant Waters of the Oasis
powers.description: Finds any natural water on the path it is travelling, by simple Perception rolls against 6, once a day on long journeys; invoked again if the water is more than half a day off (InAq; Base 2, +2 Road, +2 Smell, +2 Sun).

powers.name: Subtle Taste of Poison and Purity
powers.description: As the spell (ArM5 p. 122); poison does not harm it, a Magical Animal, so it tastes fouled water safely (InAq).

creatures.appearance: A huge white dromedary or Bactrian camel of noble bearing.
creatures.notes:
A rare master of the sands, wandering from desert to desert at the head of tribes of wild camels by way of a great Desert Regio Network linking the dry lands it calls home.

Unlike most Beasts of Virtue it lacks Susceptible to Deprivation and is immune to thirst, starvation or fatigue. Voice of the Land is entered as of the Desert. Camel is its Essential Trait.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa pp. 136-137

creatures.name: Dog, Painted (Lycaon)
creatures.how_many: Packs of one sex, up to 30
creatures.appearance: A large, lean canine with long legs and oversized round ears standing up like a wolf's. Its short mottled fur of red, black, brown, white and yellow looks painted. Its cry is more a bird's chirp than a bark.
creatures.notes:
The kalb, far more social than the small northern jackal. Packs often range near the Tuareg's desert strongholds, preying on their goats, sheep and camels, and run down gazelles and other antelope on the plains. Its habit of disembowelling prey earns its name as a killer.

Its Strength is misprinted; -3 is what its bite's Damage +1 requires (teeth +1, Crushing Jaws +3). Natural weapon: teeth Init 0, Atk +3, Def +1, Dam +1. Puissant Brawl +2 is in the block. All get +3 to running and can pursue prey long and far.

Bjornaer heartbeast: choleric with a melancholic aspect.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 137

creatures.name: Fox
creatures.appearance: Much smaller and slighter than a wolf, long in the body with a narrow head and short limbs; sandy fur and very large ears.
creatures.notes:
The tha'lab, smaller in Africa than in Europe and no less sly. Arabic stories like those of Reynard call the fox Abu Hassan or Abu Suleiman. All foxes get +3 to jumping. Natural weapon: teeth Init 0, Atk +3, Def +1, Dam +1.

The tiny fanak (fennec, Size -5, about 3 pounds) lives all over Mythic Africa and the Middle East. A larger, redder sand fox (Size -3) lives only in 'Uman: wounds adjust, combat is the same.

Cleverer foxes: Crafty x2 (Cun +3) and Guile 3 (animals). Vafer the Magical Fox and Felix the Lucky Fox are in Tales of Mythic Europe p. 14 and Magi of Hermes p. 123, a Fox of Virtue in Realms of Power: Magic p. 67. Faerie and Infernal foxes are known too.

Bjornaer heartbeast: choleric with a sanguine aspect.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 138

creatures.name: Goat (Capra)
creatures.appearance: A small wild she-goat ('anaza) such as an Arabian tahr, with short knobbly horns; males of many breeds carry larger ones.
creatures.notes:
The ma'ez. Valued for meat, milk and hairy hides, and moved between coast and mountain pasture through the year, above all in Provence and the Maghreb. Christian tales show the Devil as a black goat over a coven, folklore turns hedge magicians into goats, and moralists call them lechers for the rut.

The book's first Ability has lost its name; Athletics is entered, as every other beast's first is. Natural weapons: horns Init +1, Atk +3, Def -1, Dam +2; hooves Init +2, Atk +2, Def +2, Dam +1. All goats and sheep get +3 to climbing.

Male goat (hircus): can be larger (Size 0, Strength +2, Quickness 0), Lustful +3, Ferocity (romantic rival). Larger breeds to Size +1, the mouflon, the Levant's ibex, Morocco's Barbary sheep: large horns Init +2, Atk +3, Def +2, Dam +3.

Sheep, wild ewe (ovis): Peaceful +3, Obedient +3, no Aggressive or Extra Natural Weapons, Cunning -1 lower, Brawl (dodge) 2, usually Size -2 (Strength 2 lower, Quickness +2), not all horned. Wild ram (aries): as a male goat with Virile +3, Violent +2. Domestic goats and sheep have no Survival and Communication -4.

Bjornaer heartbeast: wild goat melancholic; wild sheep melancholic with a choleric aspect.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 138

creatures.name: Hyena (Yena)
creatures.appearance: The commoner striped hyena: a massive torso on short hind legs, so the back slopes down, and a large short-muzzled head on a long, thick, stiff neck.
creatures.notes:
The dhubba, found through the Levant, North Africa, Iraq, Persia and beyond. Striped hyenas tame and train like dogs, even joining a pack if raised with hounds; the Egyptians used them to hunt desert game. Greater African ones (Size +1) are ridden by jinn or witches, and ghuls often take the shape.

Its Social Handicap is an unpleasant odor. Natural weapon: bite Init 0, Atk +4, Def +1, Dam +3 (+6 with Crushing Jaws, p. 139).
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 139

creatures.name: Crocotta (Hyena of Virtue)
creatures.notes:
The crocotta or kynolykos (dog-wolf) of Ethiopia, thought the offspring of hyena and lion. These spotted hyenas seem to shift sex readily. They are bigger, stronger, faster and fiercer than the mundane kind, with real wits and a human-like cackle that tricks prey.

Changes from the hyena, as a template: at least Size +1, Str +4, Qik +3, Int +2, Tough Hide, Aggressive; Improved Characteristics, Tough, Tainted by Evil, Gender Shift; Brawl 5; Fierce +3 in place of Cowardly; mimicry equal to Arabic 3; all have Greater Immunity: Steel; many have Entrancement. Some strike dogs dumb with their shadow, or paralyze a creature they look at thrice.

A stone in its body, worn on the upper arm, wards against faeries of the desert or grants Premonitions or Visions; some cultures say the same of its eyes. By Persian sources a charm of its genitalia and anus gives Venus's Blessing. No full block is printed and its Might is not given.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 139

creatures.name: Jackal (Thos)
creatures.appearance: Smaller and shorter-legged than a wolf, slight, long in the body and short in the tail; mostly reddish-yellow, some marked black or grey.
creatures.notes:
The wawi or ibn 'awa, no pack animal: it hunts alone or in mated pairs or scavenges at the edge of settlements. Friendlier to man than the wolf, it can be tamed and trained as a guard, not for hunting. Black jackals are signs of Anubis, and a favoured shape of Faerie and Infernal jinn, especially ghuls, for their habit of lurking near graves.

All get +3 to running and can pursue prey long and far. Natural weapon: teeth Init 0, Atk +3, Def +1, Dam +1.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 140

creatures.name: Set Animal
creatures.notes:
The sha or sal'awa, a Typhonic beast of the easternmost deserts and Egypt: a jackal's body, a donkey's ears, a long curved snout and an upright forked tail. Tied to the dark Egyptian god Set, equated with Typhon, it foretells misfortune.

Almost surely magical, and a unique familiar for a magus who can find and befriend one, though its loyalty to a being of destruction may give pause. It may instead be a dark Faerie hound, a hedge magician's monstrous form, or an Infernal beast trying to trap a magus into serving its forgotten master.

The book prints no statistics for it. Its realm is left to the storyguide.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 140

creatures.name: Lizard, Waral (Varanus)

powers.name: Venomous Bite
powers.description: If its Attack Advantage beats the victim's armour Protection (not Soak), he suffers an exceptionally debilitating poison, Stamina against 12 or Incapacitating, whether or not the bite wounds. Boots do not stop it, and it serves well on a victim held in its locking bite.

creatures.appearance: A large grey lizard, some over 8 feet long like this one, size and colour varying with habitat. It lashes its tail when roused. Slow of gait, its powerful jaws snap shut fast to lock on prey.
creatures.notes:
The waran. Tuareg myth makes these desert lizards ancestors of the tribes, and to harm, kill or eat one is taboo. Other desert peoples think them sinister. They shelter in rock clefts and bask on flat outcrops throughout the desert.

Cunning, Communication, Soak and Survival follow the errata (p. 86). Presence is -6, or +3 for Loathsome Appearance. Ferocity defends food or a fresh kill, with Confidence 1 (3) in that only. The Bite's Damage includes +3 from Crushing Jaws (p. 139), which its Qualities do not list.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 140

creatures.name: Ostrich (Struthio)
creatures.appearance: A large bird with a long neck and legs and huge eyes. Males are typically black with white tail plumes, females a discreet grey.
creatures.notes:
The na'aam, scattered over northern Africa and commonest in Egypt; a slightly smaller kind ranges northern Arabia and the Levant. Prized for feathers and leather, less for meat, they roam the semi-arid plains in great flocks and avoid the deep desert. Hunting them is a favourite sport of nobles and rich sahirs. They cannot fly or glide, but run as fast as a gazelle (+3 to running, like horses).

Natural weapon: kick Init +2, Atk +2, Def +2, Dam +1. Thick Feathers is the catalog's Thick Fur/Thick Scales.

Some evil jinn keep bigger birds as mounts in place of horses, or trade them to nobles and sahirs who like an exotic mount: Size +2 or more, perhaps Great or Mythic Quickness, Perfect Balance and Unaffected by the Gift. Some jnun tribes have bred Faerie flocks with powers of travel and distance.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa pp. 140-141

creatures.name: Scorpion, Monstrous (Scorpio)

powers.name: Venomous Sting
powers.description: If its Attack Advantage beats the victim's armour Protection (not Soak), he suffers an exceptionally debilitating poison, Stamina against 6 or Incapacitating, whether or not the sting wounds. High leather boots and other simple measures hinder it.

creatures.appearance: A black creature with oversized pincers and an arched, barbed tail.
creatures.notes:
Al 'Aqrab, a favoured shape of evil jinn. This is the 'giant' black scorpion of the Arabian deserts, the size of a small rabbit; most are Size -8 or smaller. The book's Sting Damage has an asterisk with no note. Natural weapons: pincers Init +0, Atk +3, Def +3, Dam +4; sting Init +4, Atk +2, Def -6, Dam +1.

The lighter ones are worse, for stronger venom (at least 12, Fatal), and blending with the sand: add Camouflage, drop Aggressive, Brawl 3. Venom ranges from a Medium wound to Fatal, and even small ones may reach 15.

Larger kinds are rumoured in the deep desert: Size +3 or more guarding old tombs and sand-choked ruins in Egypt. Stories tell of winged Mesopotamian scorpion-men, scorpion-human centaurs guarding temples of old gods, and winged scorpions in Egypt and India.

Swarms (Legends of Hermes p. 44): attack with +10 damage automatically each round, Soaked normally. A normal scorpion's sting is painful and rarely fatal; the allergy that makes it fatal may be a Minor Flaw in Africa. A jinni taking the form of a swarm would suit.
creatures.source: Between Sand and Sea: Mythic Africa p. 141

creatures.name: Unicorn, Eastern (Monoceros)

powers.name: Charge of the Karkadann
powers.description: A natural power. It spends a Fatigue level to charge over flat ground with its horn, adding its Combat Ability to its Attack roll; anything smaller it strikes is knocked prone (Lords of Men p. 123).

creatures.appearance: A large grey beast with a thick armoured hide and a bull's body. A large conical horn juts from the nose and curves back above a finger-shaped lip.
creatures.notes:
The karkadann, the Lord of the Desert, of the Persian deserts and the plains of North Africa, nothing like Europe's romantic beast. Famous for charging elephants in the belly and skewering them. A virgin's care soothes it, but its horn is no antidote to poison.

It has -3 to fast or nimble movement, melee included, charging excepted. Weakness is maidens; Oversensitive, threats; Ferocity, defending territory. Its Thick Skin is the catalog's Thick Fur/Thick Scales. Natural weapons: Large Horn Init +2, Atk +3, Def +2, Dam +3; trample Init +2, Atk +2, Def +2, Dam +1. Puissant Brawl +2 is in the block. Wounds as printed: -1 (1-9), -3 (10-18), -5 (19-26), Incapacitated (27-34), Dead (35+).

Bigger ones (Size +5) and Faerie kinds live on the southern plains and foothills at the desert's edge, and the fabled Eastern Unicorn of Virtue is said to dwell in Ethiopia. Folklore tells of jinn with its head guarding the ways to Jinnistan and marching in the armies of Suleiman and Balquis. Too large for a Bjornaer heartbeast unless the magus has Giant Blood and a good story.

creatures.name: Vulture, Egyptian (Vultor)
creatures.appearance: A large ugly raptor with a bald head and bright orange face, white plumage and black-tipped wings, often fouled with blood and carrion.
creatures.notes:
The nasr, found all through the Levant, the Mythic Middle East and North Africa, called the Pharaoh's Chicken for its place in royal Egyptian carvings. Anciently tied to Isis, Mut and Nekhbet, and the sign of Upper Egypt, its wings spread over the pharaoh. Vultures are clever, breaking eggs with rocks and dropping stones on prey; the Greeks said one killed Aeschylus, taking his bald head for a tortoise.

Presence is -6, or +3 for Loathsome Appearance. The dropped stone has no Defense (n/a in the book). It counts as No Hands, -5 with stones. A half-fist stone does +3 and +1 for every two feet dropped (ArM5 p. 181), Range 10. Natural weapons: talons Init -1, Atk +2, Def +3, Dam +2; beak Init 0, Atk +3, Def +1, Dam +1; dropped stone Init 0, Atk +1, Def 0. By Pliny, +3 to smell rolls and +2 to Hunt.

Larger vultures to Size -1, slower and fiercer: Aggressive, Cunning +1, Brawl (talons) 5; they attack flamingoes and smaller creatures. Those nesting in Magic auras on remote crags warp to brilliant colours; some have Premonitions or Visions, and old females may have Divination (The Mysteries Revised Edition pp. 58-62) with Divination 4 (death), +3 to Ceremonial Augury for misfortune and +5 for death. It is a common form of ghuls and Infernal hedge wizards.

Bjornaer heartbeast: sanguine with a choleric aspect, almost always female.

creatures.name: Vulture of Virtue
creatures.appearance: A giant black vulture of the highest mountains.
creatures.notes:
They embody menace, patience and caution. Every one the magi have identified was female, and most are thought to live a hundred years. Many classical authorities deny there are male vultures, saying females bear identical daughters without a mate, an allegory the Church uses for the Virgin birth.

The skin of the bald head holds Corpus, not Animal, vis; the amount is not printed. At least one elder Bjornaer with a vulture Heartbeast has lately passed into Final Twilight as one of these, and nobody knows what a male would become.

The book prints no statistics for it.
